messages:
maria: heads up — saw a sharp p99 spike for eu-west traffic at ~16:10 UTC yesterday, p95 mostly fine. graphs: https://perf.redwood/example-chart :thinking:
jon: ok, any indication why p99 and not p95? sounds like tail / small-batch behavior or cross-region fallbacks
alex: logs show ~7.8% of requests routed to us-east due to local capacity soft-failover. those requests have much higher tail. suspect KV-cache warm/miss + small microbatches
alex: quick profiling dump (trimmed):
```
trace: kernel_choose -> kv_lookup -> wait_remote (120ms) -> kernel_smallbatch_exec (80ms)
kv_miss_rate: eu-west 9.2% -> when routed remote, kv_miss amplifies to 35%
microbatch_size median (fallbacked): 1 -> 2
```
sara: cc @maria @alex — we rolled kernel runtime change last week that optimized large-batch GEMM kernels but regressed the small-batch kernel path. could be interacting with routing fallback
maria: that fits — p95 lines up with normal local traffic. the p99 tail seems concentrated on those fallback traces.
taylor: quick experiment idea: increase min_microbatch to 4 on fallback route and prefer a quantized local variant rather than cross-region default. tradeoff: slightly higher avg latency but reduce p99 spikes
jon: can you share numbers if you ran a canary?
taylor: ran a 1h canary on a small zone (50k reqs):
- baseline (fallback->us-east): p95 120ms, p99 420ms, throughput 1000 rps
- canary (prefer_local_quantized, min_microbatch=4): p95 150ms, p99 210ms, throughput 880 rps
notes: cost per token down ~8% from quantized model, but throughput down ~12% due to batching lag
alex: that matches KV behavior — batching more before remote calls reduces remote round-trips and amortizes KV misses. kernel mismatch patch amplified the cost for tiny batches.
sara: we have two levers: (1) revert/patch small-batch kernel perf regression (eng-runtime infra PR queued), (2) adjust routing fallback heuristics to prefer local quantized variant when microbatching will be low. both together ideal
maria: ops-bot, can we schedule a targeted rollout? want to avoid changing global routing without telemetry window
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for routing-policy-change to eu-west-A (5% traffic) at 2024-12-02T09:30:00Z; will auto-rollback on p99 increase >20% over baseline
jon: also add a short-term alert: if cross-region fallback rate >5% for a region AND p99 >250ms -> page eng-runtime oncall
taylor: I'll put together a short experiment plan: compare min_microbatch 2/4/8 with prefer_local_quantized vs crossregion-default. will collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost/unit
maria: thanks. immediate owners: sara (kernel patch PR), taylor (routing canary + experiments). tagging @eng-oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
alex: tl;dr: root cause = small-batch kernel regression + KV-cache miss amplification during cross-region fallback. mitigation = prefer local quantized variant + increase microbatch threshold; long-term fix = small-batch kernel perf patch
maria: agreed. will update the incident playbook and post a short postmortem after canary finishes.
